q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution

NVIDIA will report Q2 FY2027 earnings on August 26, 2026. Today is August 19, 2026. This means resolution occurs in **7 days**.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The question asks for NVIDIA's **forward guidance** for Q2 FY2027 revenue in their Q2 FY2027 earnings release. This is critical: we already have this guidance.

According to the CURRENT RESEARCH block, NVIDIA provided forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 during their Q1 FY2027 earnings call on May 20, 2026:
- **Guidance: $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%**

This means the guided range is **$89.18 billion to $92.82 billion** (±2% of $91.0B).

The question is asking what they will announce as guidance when they report Q2 earnings on August 26, 2026. Given that they already issued this guidance in May, they will most likely **reiterate or adjust their existing guidance**.

The research also notes:
- Q1 FY2027 actual revenue was $81.6 billion
- Analyst consensus for Q2 FY2027 is $91.85 billion (slightly above guidance midpoint)
- Q3 FY2027 analyst consensus is $103.1 billion

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Execution shortfalls**: If demand for AI chips softens or supply chain issues emerge, NVIDIA could lower guidance below $89.18B
- **China revenue headwinds**: The guidance explicitly excludes China compute revenue; further restrictions could force downward revisions
- **Macro slowdown**: Any signs of customer inventory build or reduced capex spending could warrant lower guidance
- **Competitive pressures**: Increased competition from AMD or custom chips could impact demand assumptions

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Stronger-than-expected demand**: If Q2 actual results significantly exceed the $91.0B guidance midpoint, they could raise Q3 or later quarter guidance
- **Accelerating AI adoption**: Unexpected acceleration in data center spending could warrant upward revisions
- **Successful new products**: The CFO mentioned the Vera CPU opening a "$200 billion tab" — if this gains unexpected traction, guidance could increase
- **Supply chain improvements**: Better-than-expected production could support higher guidance
- **Market share gains**: If NVIDIA captures more than anticipated market share from competitors, they could raise outlook

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The CURRENT RESEARCH directly provides NVIDIA's actual guidance for Q2 FY2027: **$91.0 billion ± 2%**, which equals a range of **$89.18 billion to $92.82 billion**.

Historical precedent from the research:
- Q1 FY2027 actual: $81.6B (well within any reasonable prior guidance)
- Guidance tends to be reasonably accurate; analyst consensus at $91.85B is only $0.85B above midpoint (~0.9% deviation)

## Reasoning

With only 7 days until the earnings call, NVIDIA's guidance is already known and publicly available. The question asks what they will announce on August 26, 2026. 

Companies typically either:
1. **Reiterate guidance** when on track
2. **Raise guidance** if performing significantly better
3. **Lower guidance** if facing headwinds

Given that:
- They guided to $91.0B in May 2026
- Analyst consensus is only marginally higher at $91.85B
- No major red flags were indicated in the research
- The company has strong execution momentum (Q1 beat expectations)

The most likely outcome is that they will **reiterate guidance near $91.0 billion** or potentially **raise it slightly** to $92-93B range if Q2 results tracking shows strong performance.

The probability distribution should be centered around $91.0B with reasonable spread accounting for:
- Small upward bias (companies often beat and raise)
- The ±2% official guidance band creates natural focal points at $89.18B and $92.82B
- Some tail risk of material downward revision, but low probability given current trajectory

**Most likely single point: $91.0 billion** (their stated guidance midpoint)

**Likely range: $90.0B to $93.5B** (covering reiteration to modest raise scenarios)

**Tail risks: $88B (unexpected weakness) or $95B+ (major upside surprise)**

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is set to report its Q2 FY2027 earnings on August 26, 2026 [hudson-labs.com](https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/nvidia-q2-2027-earnings-preview-nvda-revenue-guidance-key-factors). For Q1 FY2027, reported on May 20, 2026, NVIDIA posted record revenue of $81.6 billion, with Data Center revenue at $75.2 billion [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/).

NVIDIA's guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue is $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). This guidance explicitly excludes any Data Center compute revenue from China [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027/). Analysts' consensus for Q2 FY2027 revenue is slightly higher at $91.85 billion [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/) or $91.846 billion [hudson-labs.com](https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/nvidia-q2-2027-earnings-preview-nvda-revenue-guidance-key-factors). For the subsequent quarter (Q3 FY2027), consensus revenue is $103.1 billion [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/). CFO Colette Kress anticipates $20 billion in total CPU revenue this fiscal year, with the new Vera CPU opening a "brand new $200 billion tab for Nvidia" [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027/).
